_comment: Authoritative I/O contract for every module. Do not change without notifying the whole team. See action_plan.pdf Section 9b for full explanation of each field.

module1_ocr_extraction._note: extracted_fields keys change per doc_type per config/doc_types_config.json, but the {value, confidence} wrapper shape stays identical for every field, every doc type.

flags: list of short strings, e.g. checksum_fail, expiry_passed -- empty list when clean
module2_document_validation._note: checksum_pass/text_mrz_match are null whenever no MRZ check digit could be verified for this doc_type/format — this covers mrz_format=='none', TD1 (national_id MRZ parsing is a stated, not-yet-implemented limitation), and TD3_or_none formats (e.g. visa) submitted without an MRZ at all. Not limited to mrz_format=='none' alone.

module3_tampering_detection.dl_tamper_probability: 0.0-1.0 or null if DL model unavailable - PRIMARY signal, from pretrained ManTraNet
module3_tampering_detection.ela_clarity: 0.0-1.0, how trustworthy the ELA reading itself is - feeds evidence-strength axis
module3_tampering_detection.copy_move_flag: boolean, SUPPORTING signal, geometrically-verified via RANSAC (not naive keypoint counting)
module3_tampering_detection.tamper_verdict: tampered | clean | uncertain - 'uncertain' means evidence was genuinely insufficient, this must lower evidence_strength in the risk engine, not be silently treated as clean
module3_tampering_detection._note: overall_tamper_flag is still the single boolean the risk engine's risk axis reads. tamper_verdict additionally feeds the evidence-strength axis - see docs/module3_architecture_update.md.

module4_face_verification.similarity: 0.0-1.0, or null if status is no_face_detected
module4_face_verification.doc_embedding: list[float] or null - FaceNet embedding of the document photo. Additive field (not in the original Day-2 contract): consumed by Module 6's identity_reuse_detection for cross-checkpoint nearest-neighbor search. Absent/null is safe for any consumer that doesn't need it.

module5_authority_reference_match._note: Every other module must run correctly even when this returns not_available - lets the whole pipeline work before Module 5 exists, or if it's cut entirely.

module6_blockchain_ledger.record_hash: sha256 hex string, or null if status is failed
module6_blockchain_ledger.previous_hash: sha256 hex string of prior record, or genesis value for first record, or null if status is failed
identity_reuse_matches: list of prior record IDs when identity_reuse_flag is true, empty otherwise
module6_blockchain_ledger.authority_match_status: match | mismatch | not_available | null - Module 5's status at the time this record was written, PERSISTED into the tamper-evident ledger (not just returned transiently). null means Module 5 wasn't run for this screening at all (e.g. cut entirely, or caller didn't pass authority_result) - distinct from Module 5 itself returning not_available, which is a real dict value, not a missing one.
module6_blockchain_ledger._note: final_recommendation is what the dashboard displays most prominently. authority_match_status is preserved here specifically because a Module 5 'mismatch' is the one signal that catches a flawless physical forgery - that verdict must survive in the permanent audit trail, not just appear once in an API response and be discarded. Team decision 2026-09 to formalize this into the schema (previously an undocumented additive field).

contributing_flags: list of strings explaining why the score is what it is
risk_scoring_engine._note: final_recommendation is what the dashboard displays most prominently. Dashboard should never compute this logic itself, only display it. A confident Module 5 mismatch or Module 6 identity_reuse_flag acts as a FLOOR on risk_score (forces high_risk regardless of the weighted average from Modules 2/3/4) rather than a blended weight - see risk_engine/scoring.py's module docstring for the full rationale.
